recognize_zh: 非形態學圖：左為毛細管電泳，HbA 69.2%、HbS 26.3%、HbA2 2.2%；右為 CBC，MCV 72.7 fL、MCH 22.9 pg 小球性低色素且 RBC 數偏高，HbS 比例低於一般特徵（約 35–40%），提示鐮刀型血球特質合併 α 型地中海貧血。
features: Capillary zone electrophoresis with a dominant HbA peak and a second large HbS peak (A)
Fraction table: HbA 69.2%, HbF 1.9%, HbS 26.3%, HbA2 2.2%, Z1 zone 0.4%
Normal HbA2 (2.2%), arguing against coexisting beta-thalassemia trait
CBC with RBC 5.06 x10^6/uL, Hb 11.6 g/dL, MCV 72.7 fL, MCH 22.9 pg, RDW-CV 18.8% (B)
Platelets 494 x10^3/uL with analyzer flags for anisocytosis, microcytosis, NRBC and thrombocytosis
describe_en: This figure is non-morphologic. Capillary hemoglobin zone electrophoresis (A) shows HbA 69.2%, HbS 26.3%, HbF 1.9% and HbA2 2.2%, and the automated CBC (B) shows mild microcytic hypochromic anemia with a relatively high red cell count (5.06 x10^6/uL), MCV 72.7 fL, MCH 22.9 pg, raised RDW and thrombocytosis. The presence of HbA exceeding HbS indicates sickle cell trait rather than sickle cell disease. An HbS fraction below the usual 35–40% range for trait, combined with microcytosis and normal HbA2, is consistent with coinherited alpha thalassemia; iron deficiency should be excluded and alpha-globin gene testing can confirm.

ddx.vs: HbS/beta+ thalassemia shows HbS greater than HbA with elevated HbA2 above 3.5%, whereas here HbA exceeds HbS with normal HbA2.

ddx.dx: Sickle cell trait with iron deficiency
ddx.vs: Iron deficiency also lowers the HbS fraction and MCV, but ferritin is low and the red cell count is usually reduced rather than preserved.
Uncomplicated trait has normal MCV and HbS typically 35–40%, unlike the microcytosis and 26% HbS here.
HbS/beta0 thalassemia has no HbA, with HbS predominance and raised HbA2, clearly different from this pattern.
